Section 1 · Overview

An artifact contract is a complete, Codex-actionable specification of one deliverable produced by the AbarVa platform during a Move. It tells Codex:

  • What it's called (specific name — never "the strategy doc" — always "Morgan Street Kyriba 6-Gate Remediation Roadmap")
  • Where the input data comes from (named loaded record IDs, named corpus patterns, named human inputs)
  • Which Sentinel agent generates it, in which role, using which corpus patterns, with which human-in-the-loop step
  • Who approves it (named CXO per the structure brief, or generic role for cross-tenant)
  • What format it's exported as (DOCX for memos, PDF for board packs, HTML for live dashboards, XLSX for analytical workbooks, JSON for API contracts)
  • Its evidence chain — the load-bearing chain of loaded record IDs → corpus pattern IDs → generation step IDs that lets a reader walk every claim back to its source
  • Its quality bar — the single-line acceptance criterion that distinguishes a "real" artifact from a demo-only artifact

The five locked rules (from README · operationalized here)

1
No claim without provenance

Every artifact's body text — every sentence, every number, every recommendation — must trace to one of: a loaded record (cited by table + row), a corpus pattern (cited by pattern ID), or a confirmed human input (cited by HIL prompt ID). Artifacts containing claims without provenance fail their quality bar.

2
Foundation-before-AI sequencing

Move 1 artifacts (AI capabilities) cannot be generated until Move 0 gates G1–G4 are at minimum green. Phase 5 Mobilization plans for Move 1 capabilities embed a blocked_until reference to the relevant foundation milestone. Sentinel refuses to generate downstream artifacts whose foundation is unmet.

3
No fake completion

An artifact is not "produced" until (a) its body exists, (b) its evidence chain resolves end-to-end, (c) the human-in-the-loop approval is recorded, and (d) the next-phase entry conditions are met. The Tower L0 view shows true completion state, not aspirational state. A half-approved Phase 4 business case shows as "draft", never as "done".

4
HoldCo data sovereignty

Artifacts produced from a single HoldCo's bundles are scoped to that HoldCo's tenant; L0 sees the artifact's title + status + headline metric only unless the HoldCo CXO grants drill-down. Cross-HoldCo artifacts (Move 2, 3, 4) include aggregated views by default; transaction-grain drill-down requires per-HoldCo grant.

5
No demo-only data

Every input source named in this contract maps to either a fictionalized record from the structure brief (marked as such), a corpus pattern from the loaded knowledge library, or a human input collected via the loader UI. No artifact references "data we'd have in production" — if it's not in the loader spec, it doesn't exist for Sentinel.

How Codex uses this document

  1. Pick up a Wave spec (e.g., Wave 1 spec L03 — Move 0 page)
  2. Find the relevant artifact contracts in this document (Section 3 for Move 0)
  3. For each artifact: implement input loader (Section: "Input source"), wire to the named Sentinel agent (Section: "Generation rule"), implement approval routing (Section: "Approval owner"), implement export endpoint (Section: "Export format"), build evidence chain renderer (Section: "Evidence chain"), and write the acceptance test (Section: "Quality bar")
  4. Cross-reference the pattern-setter HTML for the same Move/phase to match visual fidelity
  5. Ship as one PR per spec, per the Wave map in 02-demo-spine-architecture.html §13

Section 2 · The contract schema

Every artifact row in Sections 3–7 contains these seven columns. Below: the schema definitions, then one annotated worked example.

1 · Artifact name
Specific, never generic. Names follow the pattern <Tenant> <Subject> <Type>. Examples: "Morgan Street Banking H2H Connectivity Matrix" (good); "banking doc" (bad). The name is the user-facing title and the file-system stem of any exported artifact.
2 · Input source
A bullet list of named inputs in one of three forms:
  • loader.<bundle>.<table>[filter] — references a specific table loaded by a specific CXO bundle (see 03-cxo-intel-loader-spec.html)
  • CORPUS-PATTERN-ID — references a specific pattern from the loaded knowledge library
  • HIL.<prompt-id> — references a specific human-in-the-loop input prompt
3 · Generation rule
Specifies (a) the Sentinel agent role responsible — SentinelTreasury, SentinelArchitect, SentinelFinance, SentinelProcurement, SentinelRisk, SentinelPortfolio; (b) the model role within that agent (diagnose, draft, score, summarize); (c) the corpus patterns it draws on; (d) the human-in-the-loop step that confirms before finalization.
4 · Approval owner
A specific named role from the structure brief for HoldCo-scoped artifacts (e.g., "Aisha Vargas — Morgan Street Group Treasurer"). A generic role for cross-tenant artifacts (e.g., "L0 Operating Partner — Technology"). Artifacts requiring multi-party sign-off list all approvers and the order.
5 · Export format
DOCX (long-form memos, strategy docs, mobilization plans) · PDF (board packs, IC papers, regulatory artifacts) · HTML (live dashboards, scorecards, evidence views) · XLSX (analytical workbooks, business cases, vendor matrices) · JSON (API contracts, Source event payloads). Format matches actual consumption pattern, not platform default.
6 · Evidence chain
The artifact's provenance: loaded record IDs (table + key) + corpus pattern IDs + generation step IDs from prior artifacts. Renders in the UI as a "show provenance" panel; each cited element is clickable and resolves to the source. Required for compliance with rule 1.
7 · Quality bar
One sentence describing what makes this artifact "real" — the acceptance test. Used in CI: a tagged eval harness produces the artifact against the demo seed; if the output fails the quality bar test, the build fails.

Annotated example

This is one row from Section 3 (Move 0 G1 Phase 1 Discovery), broken out and explained inline. Every subsequent row follows the same shape, presented in compact table form.

Artifact (1 · name)

Morgan Street Banking H2H Connectivity Matrix — a per-bank scorecard showing H2H readiness, current connectivity method, daily file integrity, and remediation priority for all 14 banks in the Morgan Street relationship inventory.

Input source (2)
  • loader.cfo.banking_relationships[tenant=morgan-street] — 14 rows, one per bank, with services, fee structure, H2H readiness flag, annual fee
  • loader.cio.application_inventory[category=treasury] — Kyriba record with current connector mode
  • CORPUS-FINSERV-08-BANKING-COST-TO-INCOME — benchmark anchor for "what good looks like" on bank rationalization
  • CORPUS-FINSERV-13-IT-SPEND-MIDMARKET — IT spend benchmarks anchoring "is this in range"
  • HIL.kyriba-rollout-status — Aisha Vargas confirms current per-bank go-live status
Generation rule (3)

SentinelTreasury in diagnose role. Prompts: "Given the 14 banking relationships and Kyriba's current H2H mode, produce a per-bank readiness scorecard. For each bank, classify connectivity as H2H-live / H2H-ready-not-live / portal-scrape / manual. Cite each classification to a specific loaded record. Cite the rationalization benchmark to FINSERV-08." Corpus patterns: FINSERV-08, FINSERV-13. HIL gate: HIL.kyriba-rollout-status — Aisha Vargas confirms or corrects the inferred status before Sentinel finalizes.

Approval owner (4)

Aisha Vargas — Morgan Street Group Treasurer (primary). Sarah Lindqvist — CFO (secondary, view-only for awareness). Approval route: /moves/move-0/morgan-street/g1/banking-matrix/approve.

Export format (5)

HTML live dashboard (primary, refreshes when bank records change) + XLSX exportable scorecard (for Treasurer's offline review, weekly cadence). No PDF — this is operational, not board-pack.

Evidence chain (6)

Per-bank-row provenance: loader.cfo.banking_relationships[id=<bank_id>] → readiness classification rule → FINSERV-08 benchmark cite. Aggregate-row provenance: weighted-sum across 14 rows + FINSERV-13 rationalization range. Every cell exposes a "show provenance" affordance that resolves to the underlying record.

Quality bar (7)

A treasury professional reading this matrix can identify, without further questions, which banks block H2H rollout, what the remediation step is per bank, and what the projected fee compression is when rationalized to the target 6 — with every number sourced.

Every artifact in Sections 3–7 is specified to this level of detail, presented in compact-table form for density. When implementing, Codex expands the table row back to this card form.

Section 3 · Move 0 — Kyriba De-Risk (per HoldCo)

Scope: per HoldCo where a platform rollout is in flight. Six gates (G1–G6) × six phases (P0–P5). Primary demo tenant: Morgan Street. Artifact owner across the Move: Group Treasurer (Aisha Vargas for Morgan Street). ~20 artifacts total.

Move 0 anchoring. Every Move 0 artifact references the 6-gate table from the structure brief. The gates are the canonical structure; the phases (P0 Setup through P5 Mobilization) are the lifecycle each gate moves through. Most gates produce 2–4 artifacts across phases.

Section 4 · Move 1 — AI on top of Kyriba (per HoldCo)

Scope: per HoldCo, post-Move 0 G1–G4 minimum green. Four AI capabilities × six phases. Lakefront's deployed models are case-study evidence. Primary demo tenant: Morgan Street (rollout target).

Foundation gate. Every Move 1 artifact carries a blocked_until reference to the Move 0 milestone its data plane depends on. Sentinel refuses to draft a Phase 5 mobilization for any capability whose foundation isn't met.

Section 10 · Provenance + evidence chain rules

This section operationalizes locked rule 1: no claim without provenance. Every artifact's body text must thread back. Here are the rules, the failure modes, and three concrete worked examples.

Rules

A
Every numeric claim cites a source

Any number in artifact body (count, amount, percentage, ratio) must trace to: a loaded record (table.column.row), a corpus pattern's stated benchmark range, or a HIL-confirmed human input. No "approximately", no unsourced rounded numbers.

B
Every recommendation cites a rationale chain

"We recommend X" must be followed (in the evidence panel, not necessarily inline) by: the discovery finding that drove X + the pattern or benchmark that validates X as the right move + the foundation X depends on (if any).

C
Cross-tenant cites carry grant logs

Any claim in an L0 or cross-HoldCo artifact that uses a specific HoldCo's transaction-grain data carries the grant log entry that authorized the read. Without it, the claim is redacted to aggregate.

D
"I don't know" is a valid Sentinel output

If a claim would have no provenance, Sentinel emits "I need <named input> to answer this — please load it via <named loader UI route>". This is not a failure; it's the system honoring rule 1.

E
Evidence panel is co-rendered, never optional

Every artifact's UI renders an "evidence" panel showing the full chain. The panel is collapsible but never absent. Exported DOCX/PDF includes an appendix with the same chain in printed form.

Failure modes (what gets caught in eval)

  • Unsourced number — fails CI eval (every artifact in seed produced and chain-walked)
  • Pattern cited but inapplicable — eval checks pattern.applies_to matches artifact tenant + Move + phase
  • Cross-tenant claim without grant — RLS prevents data access; chain validator confirms grant log timestamp pre-dates artifact
  • Broken chain — referenced artifact ID doesn't resolve; eval fails
  • Stale loader data — chain step shows loader record age > configured freshness threshold; artifact downgraded to draft

Three worked examples

Claim: "Morgan Street's bank rationalization to 6 strategic banks would unlock $2.8M annual fee compression."

Discovery finding: loader.cfo.banking_relationships[tenant=morgan-street] = 14 rows with per-bank annual fee totaling current spend
Benchmark: CORPUS-FINSERV-08 banking cost-to-income, mid-market rationalization range 18–22% on consolidated spend
Computation: $14.3M current consolidated banking fees × 20% midpoint = $2.86M (rounded to $2.8M, in-range claim)
HIL confirmation: HIL.kyriba-rollout-status · Aisha Vargas confirmed 4 H2H-ready banks at 2026-06-04T14:22Z
Used in artifact: M0-P1-G1-A02 Bank Rationalization Brief (Move 0 · Phase 1 · G1)
Verdict: Chain resolves. Range cited honestly (point estimate within range; not the top of range).

Claim: "Lakefront's deployed payment anomaly model achieves <2% false-positive rate after 6 months of tuning."

Source: loader.cio.ai_production_workloads[tenant=lakefront, workload=payment-anomaly] · realized FPR field
Cross-tenant grant log: Yuki Ono (Lakefront CIO) granted Move 1 read on AI workload records at 2026-06-01T10:00Z (logged in cross_tenant_grants)
HIL confirmation: HIL.lakefront-grant · Yuki Ono confirmed claim attribution before publication
Used in artifact: M1-P2-A01 AI Portfolio Memo · cited as case-study evidence
Verdict: Chain resolves. Cross-tenant grant present. Claim is attributed not generalized ("Lakefront's deployed model" not "models in general").

Claim: "Microsoft EA federation across 3 HoldCos would yield $1.0–1.4M annual cost compression."

Discovery finding: loader.cio.major_vendor_contracts[vendor=Microsoft EA] across 3 HoldCos · $4.2M + $2.1M + $2.8M = $9.1M consolidated
Benchmark range: CORPUS-FINSERV-13 + CORPUS-FINSERV-20 + Gartner enterprise-rate-tier compression 11–15% on $9M+ consolidated EA spend
Computation: $9.1M × [11%, 15%] = [$1.0M, $1.4M] · output is a range (not a point) per rule A
Cross-tenant grant log: 3 HoldCo CIOs granted Move 2 read on major-vendor-contract data at separate timestamps (logged)
Used in artifact: M2-P1-A02 Top-20 Scorecard · M2-P4-A01 Biz Case · L-S02 Source spawn
Verdict: Chain resolves end-to-end. Range honest. Cross-tenant grants present. No double-counting (single Microsoft EA per HoldCo).

Appendix I · Codex implementation checklist (per artifact)

When picking up any artifact contract, Codex confirms the following checklist before claiming the artifact "ready". This list is the operationalization of every artifact row in Sections 3-7.

  1. Surface route exists. The artifact has a named app route (e.g., /moves/move-0/morgan-street/g1/banking-matrix) and a named approval route (e.g., the same path + /approve).
  2. Input loader wired. Every loader.<bundle>.<table> referenced resolves to a real query against the data plane; missing tables raise a typed error, not silent empty results.
  3. Sentinel agent invoked. The named SentinelAgent is invoked with the specified model role; the agent's prompt template references the specified corpus patterns.
  4. HIL prompt rendered (where applicable). Each HIL prompt has a UI surface; HIL confirmation is logged to the evidence chain table; the artifact cannot move from draft to final without HIL completion.
  5. Approval route wired. Approval routes to the named CXO; CXO identity comes from the tenant context (not hardcoded); approval is logged with timestamp.
  6. Export endpoint produces correct format. Endpoint produces the specified format (DOCX/PDF/HTML/XLSX/JSON); a CI test asserts file produces and validates.
  7. Evidence chain panel renders. Every artifact UI exposes the evidence chain panel; each cited loader record + corpus pattern + HIL prompt is clickable and resolves.
  8. Quality bar test passes. A tagged CI eval (see Appendix G) runs the artifact against the demo seed and validates the quality bar; failure breaks the build.
  9. Foundation gate honored. If the artifact depends on a Move 0 foundation (Move 1 artifacts), Sentinel refuses to generate the artifact when the foundation gate is not green.
  10. Cross-tenant sovereignty enforced. If the artifact references HoldCo-other-than-self data, the cross-tenant grant log is checked before render; absent grants downgrade the artifact to aggregate-only.
  11. Refresh + freshness semantics implemented. Each artifact has a defined refresh cadence (real-time / daily / weekly / quarterly); stale loader records (older than configured threshold) downgrade artifact to draft.
  12. Source spawn JSON conforms (where applicable). Spawn artifacts produce JSON validating against the Source module's intake schema (see §9 spawn schema). The Source module accepts the payload and lands the event in Stage 5.

Appendix K · Glossary

L0 / L1 / L2
L0 = sponsor (Lakeshore) · L1 = HoldCo (Morgan Street, Roosevelt, Lakefront) · L2 = PortCo (24 underlying companies)
HoldCo
Holding company; L1 tenant in this demo
PortCo
Portfolio company owned by an L1 HoldCo
Move
Workflow-anchored AI strategy track. Five canonical Moves in this demo: M0 Kyriba De-Risk, M1 AI on top of Kyriba, M2 Cross-HoldCo Cost Reduction, M3 Federated IT Strategy, M4 Federated Risk + Governance
Phase (P0..P5)
Each Move runs through phases: P0 Setup load, P1 Discovery, P2 Strategy, P3 Architecture, P4 Business case, P5 Mobilization
Gate (G1..G6)
Move 0 specific: the six platform-rollout de-risk gates (Banking connectivity, ERP feed quality, Entity hierarchy, Position reconstruction, User adoption, IC auto-reconciliation)
Capability (Cap 1..Cap 4)
Move 1 specific: the four AI capabilities (Cash forecast, Payment anomaly/BEC, Covenant headroom, IC auto-reconciliation)
L-S01..L-S07
Lakeshore Source event identifiers; spawned from Move Phase 3 Architecture phases when procurement is in scope
CXO Intel Loader
The five per-CXO upload bundles (CIO, CFO, COO, CHRO, GC) that onboard a HoldCo onto AbarVa. Specified in 03-cxo-intel-loader-spec.html
Sentinel
The orchestrator agent fronting Source and Intelligence surfaces (per memory note on workflow-first agents). In this package: SentinelTreasury, SentinelFinance, SentinelArchitect, SentinelProcurement, SentinelRisk, SentinelPortfolio are the named front agents
Atlas
The orchestrator agent fronting Tower surfaces. L0 Federated Command Center is Atlas-fronted
HIL (Human-in-the-loop)
Pre-finalization confirmation by a named human before Sentinel emits an artifact. Registry in Appendix E
Evidence chain
The provenance trail tied to every artifact: loaded record IDs + corpus pattern IDs + HIL confirmation logs. Operationalized in Section 10
Foundation-before-AI
Locked rule 2: Move 1 (AI) artifacts cannot ship until their Move 0 (foundation) gates are green. Phase 5 mobilization plans embed blocked_until milestones referencing the foundation gate
Sovereignty
Locked rule 4: HoldCo data is scoped to its tenant; L0 sees aggregates; sibling HoldCos cannot read each other's transaction-grain without explicit grant. Enforced via holding_group_id RLS and grant log
Pattern setter
The full-fidelity reference HTMLs in this package: 07 (Move 0 Kyriba), 08 (Move 2 vendor), 09 (business case canonical), 10 (mobilization canonical). They define visual + content fidelity bar
